references.text: The prophet Isaiah speaks of a holy way, 'the Way of Holiness,' which the unclean shall not walk on, reminiscent of the narrow path Jesus mentions.
Proverbs presents the contrast between the way of the righteous, which is like the morning light, and the way of the wicked, which is dark; parallel to the narrow and broad paths.
The book of Psalms speaks of the Lord's way versus the way of the ungodly, which can be seen as a precursor to Jesus' teaching about the two ways.
Hebrews encourages pursuing peace with everyone and striving for holiness, which can be connected to choosing the narrow path.
In Revelation it is mentioned that nothing unclean shall enter the new Jerusalem, which can be related to the necessity of choosing the narrow path to attain salvation.
